REQ-collector-crypt-adapter-1.title: Collector Crypt documented response contract
REQ-collector-crypt-adapter-1.statement: Given a Collector Crypt pack or buyback response, when the adapter validates it, then prize tiers are numeric 1 through 4, buyback amounts are configured Solana stablecoin base units with six decimals, contains accepts an integer or numeric string, and openPack uses the documented idempotent operation. insured_value is usable only when reconciliation proves its unit against the machine instantBuyback percentage; otherwise the card becomes a HELD_DATA_UNVERIFIED held position. Edge case: an unsupported tier, malformed contains value, non-idempotent open result, missing unit proof, or reconciliation mismatch cannot authorize purchase, sale, or payout.
REQ-collector-crypt-adapter-1.measurement: Adapter and lifecycle fixtures cover all four tiers, integer and numeric-string contains values, documented idempotent openPack replay, configured Solana stablecoin base-unit accounting, insured-value reconciliation, and a HELD_DATA_UNVERIFIED held position on every missing or contradictory proof.

REQ-cycle-repository-1.title: One authoritative journaled cycle repository
REQ-cycle-repository-1.statement: Given any money mutation, when a dashboard, CLI, scheduler, public projection, or runner stage requests it, then one CycleRepository and policy engine are the sole authority for state and every client uses its durable transitions. A provider attempt is write-ahead PREPARED, then NOT_SENT for a pre-call failure with no provider contact and retry permission, SENT_UNKNOWN for post-send ambiguity with observation only, or RESPONSE_RECORDED followed by RECONCILED. A card-level buyback, open, or epic-gate hold creates an attributed HeldPosition `{positionId, cycleId, packId, memo, mint, cardRef, costMicroUsd, insuredValue, reason, terminalState, evidenceDigest, openedAtMs, ownerDecision, resolution}`; `insuredValue` is a typed amount or null. A card attempt that remains SENT_UNKNOWN past `unresolvedCardDeadlineMinutes` (default 30, minimum 5, maximum 1440) opens the same kind of position. A position stores its attributed purchase cost in USD micro-units. Insured amounts remain informational and never replace attributed purchase cost for held controls; a Solana stablecoin amount is never assumed equal to USD. Historical committed purchase costs are not revalued when ETH moves. It remains in its own custody bucket while the cycle retains only settled cards, and a cycle may become COMPLETED with open positions, including an all-held cycle with zero proceeds and a zero payout manifest. COMPLETED retains open positions for supplementary recovery; `readActiveCycle` skips it for scheduler admission, but it remains an active DurableCycleStore entry until position resolution. The 16-entry store supports the default `maxHeldPositions` 10 when positions span completed cycles; a configuration above that verified-safe value of 10 is refused at admission until post-completion position archival or a measured store-capacity exemption exists. The first accepted `sell` decision for a position atomically creates exactly one supplementary settlement keyed by `positionId`; an exact replay of that same request returns the identical settlement, a conflicting or later `sell` request for an already-settled or in-flight position fails, and a resolved position (`SOLD`, `REFUNDED`, or `NEVER_SENT`) can never create another settlement. That settlement captures the original completed eligibility-snapshot evidence as `eligibilitySnapshotEvidenceDigest`; at `RETURN_BROADCAST`, the repository derives an immutable `payoutSourceDigest` from that position's finalized USDG return and return binding with zero/null supplementary dust, and binds that finalized return and any permitted dust source to a one-time atomic consumption record shared by every supplementary manifest for that position, so at most one supplementary manifest is ever created per held position and per return source. A nonzero supplementary dust source requires that same atomic, position-aware consumption transition before it can be used. A supplementary payout accepts only those persisted identities; `keep-holding` has no settlement effect. Repository evidence can close an overdue unresolved position as sold, refunded, or never sent with durable evidence. Production observation-only provider reconciliation and automatic supplementary intent are required before that resolution is automated. The card-level carve-out never applies to a semantic-invalid whole-cycle class: a wrong-asset or wrong-recipient transaction-policy refusal, cross-cycle attribution failure, conflicting canonical evidence, an unattributed deposit, missing predecessor evidence, or snapshot failure remain terminal whole-cycle `HELD_*` states with an owner decision. A durable chain attempt is PREPARED(requestDigest, policyDigest, fencingToken), then SIGNED(rawSignedBytesHash, nonceOrBlockhash, txHash, approvedSemanticsDigest), BROADCAST, FINALIZED, or REFUSED(reason, fencingToken). Raw signed bytes remain immutably retrievable by their content address. A RelayLegV1 persists cycleId, direction, relayRequestId, quoteDigest, both chain transaction hashes, typed source and destination amounts, both finality observations, and netDeltaAtomic. A source or destination transaction hash attributes to exactly one relay leg across all cycles and directions. A leg is SETTLED only after this process observes both finalized deltas through its own RPC clients and attributes the destination delta by amount, time window, and memo or relayRequestId; Relay status alone cannot settle it. Partial, refund, late, and wrong-asset outcomes enter respectively HELD_RELAY_PARTIAL, HELD_RELAY_REFUND, HELD_RELAY_LATE, and HELD_RELAY_WRONG_ASSET. A StandingAuthorityDecisionV1 atomically persists authorityDigest, verifiedAt, intentDigest, dayCapReservation, and nonceReservation on first use after a wall-clock expiry check; an expired authority is refused and replay is idempotent. CycleRecord persists immutable production or rehearsal mode. The custody ledger separates finalized observed balances from obligations, counts unresolved principal exactly once, and classifies expected cycle assets separately from unattributed external deposits that pause new claims. Each transition is written before its irreversible effect; restart revalidates the persisted approvedSemanticsDigest before any rebroadcast and never creates a new nonce, blockhash, bytes, or signature while unresolved. Edge case: timeout, disconnect, or 5xx after send is SENT_UNKNOWN and supports observation only.
REQ-cycle-repository-1.measurement: Node tests inject crashes at every transition, pre-call failures, lost responses, concurrent clients, fencing contention, cross-mode service calls, nonce contention, external deposits, and state recovery. They assert one durable store, write-ahead ordering, byte-identical rebroadcast after approval-digest revalidation, exact unresolved-principal accounting, no duplicate effect, cross-cycle relay-hash rejection, dual-RPC settlement, destination attribution, named relay recovery states, atomic standing-authority reservations, wall-clock expiry refusal, idempotent authority replay, card-level hold carving, the SENT_UNKNOWN deadline and its sold, refunded, and never-sent outcomes, snapshot- and source-bound supplementary settlement restart recovery, all-held zero completion, no inter-cycle custody mixing, exactly one settlement per positionId across restart, an exact replay of the same sell request ID with identical evidence returning the identical settlement, a sell request with a different request ID after the first accepted sell failing without creating or funding a second settlement, a sell attempted after resolution failing, a configuration above the verified-safe held-position capacity being refused at admission, and every named semantic-invalid class (wrong-asset, wrong-recipient, cross-cycle attribution failure, conflicting canonical evidence, unattributed deposit, missing predecessor evidence, snapshot failure) keeping its terminal whole-cycle hold unchanged.

REQ-cycle-repository-2.title: Bounded transient recovery classification
REQ-cycle-repository-2.statement: Given a provider or chain attempt that fails before, during, or after an external effect, when the repository classifies its recovery path, then it assigns exactly one of three classes: semantic-invalid (the request itself is wrong and requires a terminal HELD_* state with an owner decision), effect-ambiguous (the external outcome cannot yet be distinguished and the attempt stays observation-only until canonical evidence resolves it), or proven-pre-effect-transient (no external effect occurred and the identical approved intent may retry automatically once the blocking condition clears). A Relay quote that expires before any request or signature is proven-pre-effect-transient: it stays nonterminal with no cycle terminal state and no attempt, persists the expired quote identity and deadline, and only after re-proving no signed or broadcast attempt exists does policy/admission atomically select one replacement quote for the same claimed principal under `refresh-after-readmission`; it never silently substitutes a quote once signed bytes exist. A Solana chain attempt whose blockhash expires past its validity boundary is effect-ambiguous: it stays `BROADCAST` and observation-only until reconciliation either finalizes it or produces canonical expired-and-unlanded proof, and only then creates exactly one linked replacement attempt with a fresh blockhash under `reconcile-then-replace`, retaining the original signed bytes and signature permanently. A wallet lease or fencing token lost strictly before the provider or signature capability boundary is proven-pre-effect-transient: it stays `NOT_SENT` with no cycle terminal state, and a newly fenced owner may retry the identical prepared request digest exactly once under `retry-same-request-under-new-lease`. Lease loss discovered after a provider-mutation capability boundary was already reached is a distinct, effect-ambiguous class: it is reclassified `SENT_UNKNOWN`, stays observation-only under `reconcile-before-retry`, and forbids any automatic retry or new provider mutation until canonical reconciliation resolves the prior attempt; it never shares the pre-boundary class's tuple. Lease loss discovered after a signing capability boundary was already reached is instead governed by the durable chain-attempt contract's own `PREPARED`/`SIGNED`/`BROADCAST`/`REFUSED` states from REQ-cycle-repository-1, not by `SENT_UNKNOWN`, because a chain attempt already carries its own state machine for that ambiguity. An external signer denial that provably occurred before any signature could have been produced is proven-pre-effect-transient: it stays `NOT_SENT` with no cycle terminal state, persists a bounded redacted signer-unavailable reason and next retry time, and retries the identical request against the same approved signer identity after bounded backoff under `retry-after-signer-readiness`. A sign-only external signer timeout may retry the identical signing attempt only for the verified owned Keychain broker, whose separate, distinctly guarded broadcast capability the checked-in source proves its sign operation never reaches. That retry is proven-pre-effect-transient only when the exact unsigned wire bytes, signer role/account identity, request digest, policy/authorization digest, and validity context were durably persisted before that broker's sign-only operation was first invoked; the retry reuses those exact durably bound values, never regenerates the provider transaction, blockhash, nonce, memo, or policy under the retry's identity, and never asserts the prior attempt produced no signature — a signature returned by either attempt is captured exactly once through the existing signed-bytes recovery record, which rejects materially different signing material, under `retry-sign-only-with-durable-binding`. This identical-byte, idempotent-retry guarantee is enabled only once focused evidence proves it for that exact broker contract; it grants no broadcast authority, and a subsequent broadcast or provider-send outcome that cannot be distinguished remains its own observation-only `SENT_UNKNOWN` or chain-attempt state, never retried as an unsigned request. Every opaque or external-module signer timeout keeps the existing no-automatic-retry, terminal whole-cycle class, because canonical chain observation cannot recover or rule out an unbroadcast signature for it; automatic sign-only retry is not extended to any other signer by this revision, and a future signer can receive it only through a later owner-approved spec revision bound to that exact signer contract, never by an implementation-time claim of equivalence. Edge case: a stale fenced owner performs no effect after fence failure; a class assignment never exports a key, substitutes a signer, or creates a new request; and semantic-invalid classes (wrong-asset, wrong-recipient, cross-cycle attribution failure, conflicting canonical evidence) keep their existing terminal HELD_* owner-decision contract unchanged.
REQ-cycle-repository-2.measurement: Node tests prove each named failure class retries or replaces only under its assigned class's proven condition, that a pre-effect retry uses the identical request digest and an effect-ambiguous case never retries blindly, that lease loss after a provider-mutation boundary uses SENT_UNKNOWN while lease loss after a signing boundary uses the chain-attempt state machine instead, that a signer timeout is never treated identically to a provable pre-signature denial, that the sign-only retry guarantee is exercised only for the verified Keychain broker contract with its exact unsigned bytes, signer identity, request digest, policy digest, and validity context durably bound before invocation and reused unchanged on retry, that no retry ever regenerates a provider transaction, blockhash, nonce, memo, or policy, that a signature from either attempt is deduplicated by the existing signed-bytes recovery record, that an opaque or external-module signer's timeout keeps the current no-automatic-retry terminal class, that broadcast/provider-send ambiguity is asserted separately as SENT_UNKNOWN or a chain-attempt state and never retried as an unsigned request, that quote and lease replacement never occurs while signed or broadcast evidence is unresolved, that the Solana replacement attempt is singular and linked with the original signature retained, that the signer-unavailable reason is redacted and durable across restart, and that the existing wrong-asset, wrong-recipient, and other semantic-invalid HELD_* contracts are unchanged.

REQ-cycle-runner-3.title: Cycle-attributed operations-wallet stages
REQ-cycle-runner-3.statement: Given a planned cycle, when the runner executes it, then its ordered stages are eligibility-snapshot, claim-process, outbound, purchase, open, epic-gate, buyback, return, and payout. The runner persists the immutable cycle mode before stage execution and production services refuse rehearsal cycles while rehearsal services refuse production cycles. Before signing a purchase, it persists typed {chainId, assetId, decimals, amountAtomic} values for unitPriceAtomic, totalAtomic, and boundedOverheadAtomic plus positive integer-string quantity; totalAtomic equals quantity multiplied by unitPriceAtomic, all money fields share the same asset identity, and policy reserves totalAtomic plus boundedOverheadAtomic. A card carved into a held position no longer keeps the cycle terminally held. Return and the main payout bridge and distribute only settled, cycle-attributed proceeds, list excluded positions in their evidence, and allow COMPLETED with open positions or a zero-proceeds, zero-manifest COMPLETED result when every card is held. A completed record with open positions remains one active DurableCycleStore entry for supplementary recovery even though scheduler admission skips it. The 16-entry store supports the default `maxHeldPositions` 10 when positions span completed cycles; a configuration above that verified-safe value of 10 is refused at admission until post-completion position archival or a measured store-capacity exemption exists. Outbound can use only the cycle's claimed principal. No bucket can fund another cycle. The custody ledger records finalized observed current balances separately from obligations, counts unresolved principal exactly once, records expected cycle assets separately from unattributed external deposits, and pauses new claims for those deposits. For the canonical EVM native ETH row only, hookemon.custody-ledger.v3 with an independently finalized native balance observation carries a verifiedCurrentBalance (CustodyBalanceObservationV1 | null) and a singular expectedCycleAsset (TypedAmount | null, never a collection), and unvaluedExposure becomes true whenever verifiedCurrentBalance is null while unresolved principal is positive or any current-custody bucket is nonzero. A pure, two-independent-source finalized-observation combiner (packages/adapters/src/solana-custody-balance-observation.mjs#combineFinalizedBalanceObservation and #observeFinalizedBalanceWithRetry) is an allowed evidence-construction contract for a future non-EVM verifiedCurrentBalance; it is not itself a durable producer, a canonical chain/asset identity source, a custody-ledger writer, a valuation, or live readiness proof, and constructing its output does not by itself satisfy this requirement. Any non-native-EVM row stays on hookemon.custody-ledger.v1, or, if migrated to v2, stays permanently unvalued and fail-closed under the same admission rule until a separately approved evidence producer exists for it. Native principal and gas share the ETH asset identity but occupy separate reservation and cost buckets; spendable principal excludes the gas reserve and unpaid obligations. Only finalized cycle-attributed native payment proofs may become an Operations ETH credit or payout basis. A direct native payment is proved from the persisted signed transaction identity, exact sender, recipient, value and calldata, successful receipt and canonical finalized block; a trusted hook post-payment event proves a claim. Internal Relay return or refund proof additionally authenticates emitter runtime, request linkage, decoded recipient/value and failure propagation. Missing proof leaves proceeds unavailable. No wallet-wide delta or fabricated ERC20 Transfer event proves a native credit. Historical USDG journals remain readable but cannot resume through the native runtime or be rescaled; native cycles use fresh identities. Edge case: an unattributed inbound deposit, cross-mode request, mismatched purchase total, bridge-funded cross-cycle action, a non-native-EVM v2 row treated as valued without an approved producer, or attempt to finance one cycle with another fails closed.
REQ-cycle-runner-3.measurement: End-to-end fakes and fork tests assert exact nine-stage order, typed-amount validation, purchase arithmetic and reserve, immutable mode isolation, held-position carve-out, settled-proceeds-only return and payout, all-held zero completion, completed-record supplementary recovery without reopening the main cycle, interleaved-cycle isolation, asset separation, cycle-attribution keys, claimed-principal-only outbound, proceeds-delta-only return, finality before completion, observed-balance and obligation conservation, one-time unresolved-principal accounting, pause on unattributed deposits, and independent gas reserves; custody-ledger fixtures additionally prove the EVM native ETH row's unvaluedExposure admission rule on a null verifiedCurrentBalance with nonzero unresolved claim or current-custody bucket, the singular non-collection expectedCycleAsset write-time refusal of a second unresolved return leg, and that a non-native-EVM row constructed as v2 remains permanently unvalued absent an approved producer. Native tests reject wrong request/emitter/runtime/value, failed internal calls, unrelated deposits, stale or reorged receipts, duplicate proofs, old USDG resume and any principal spending that consumes the gas reserve.

REQ-direct-payout-1.title: Finalized direct holder payout
REQ-direct-payout-1.statement: Given a finalized cycle-attributed Operations native ETH credit and its frozen eligibility manifest, when the main payout begins, then the runner sends direct native ETH value payments only for settled cards through the durable chain-attempt contract: PREPARED(requestDigest, policyDigest, fencingToken), SIGNED(rawSignedBytesHash, nonceOrBlockhash, txHash, approvedSemanticsDigest), BROADCAST, FINALIZED, or REFUSED(reason, fencingToken). The first accepted sell decision for one held position atomically creates exactly one supplementary settlement keyed by that position's ID, starting a supplementary buyback, return leg for only that position's attributed proceeds, and supplementary payout with manifest ID `<cycleId>:supplementary:<n>`; an exact replay of that same sell request returns the identical settlement and manifest identifier, a conflicting or later sell request for an already-settled or in-flight position fails, and a resolved position can never create a second manifest. The settlement persists the digest of the original completed eligibility snapshot; its RETURN_BROADCAST boundary persists the exact finalized return and return binding as a payout-source digest, and binds that return and any permitted dust source to a one-time atomic consumption record shared across every supplementary manifest for that position, so at most one supplementary manifest is ever funded per held position and per return source. The supplementary payout accepts only that snapshot and source, becomes immutable at its first broadcast, and pays every recipient exactly once for that manifest. It uses zero/null dust unless that same atomic position-aware supplementary dust-consumption transition has bound an unconsumed original-cycle source. The wallet-wide nonce lock covers claim, outbound, return, main payout, and supplementary payout. SIGNED records retain immutable retrievable signed bytes and recover after restart. A dropped BROADCAST resolves by receipt search or a replacement using the same nonce and calldata, after revalidating the persisted approvedSemanticsDigest. It marks paid only after proof of the exact successful finalized transaction matched to persisted signed bytes/hash, source, recipient, value and calldata; a recipient may forward ETH and its ending balance is not payment proof. Rejected recipient calls become quarantine liabilities without blocking the rest of a manifest; dust carry is durable and atomically consumed and written between cycles. Edge case: a crash between supplementary broadcast and finality, duplicate recipient, nonce collision, replacement with different calldata, changed approval digest, dropped broadcast, rejecting recipient, or dust replay cannot create a double payment or silently change either manifest.
REQ-direct-payout-1.measurement: Node tests cover restart at every main and supplementary payout boundary, durable signed-record recovery, approval-digest revalidation, exact finalized native transaction identity, value and successful execution, immutable manifests, the original snapshot and return source reused by a supplementary manifest, exactly-once supplementary transfers after restart, exactly one settlement and manifest per positionId across restart, an exact replay of the same sell request ID with identical evidence returning the identical settlement and manifest identifier, a sell request with a different request ID after the first accepted sell failing without creating or funding a second manifest, a second manifest attempted for the same position/return source failing, same-nonce-and-calldata replacement, receipt search for a dropped broadcast, wallet-wide nonce fencing, refusal fencing, rejecting-recipient quarantine with continuation, failed gas counted as cost rather than principal, and no automatic retry, redirect or WETH fallback for terminal REFUSED recipients, durable dust carry, and recipient counts through the verified feasibility envelope.

REQ-eligibility-snapshot-1.title: Pre-claim finalized eligibility snapshot
REQ-eligibility-snapshot-1.statement: Given a planned cycle, when eligibility-snapshot runs as the first cycle stage, then before claimProcess the runner pins a finalized block and hash, replays HKMN Transfer logs from deployment through that block, reconciles mint minus burn against the launch manifest, rechecks the block hash after scanning, and proves log completeness through an independent second source or archive RPC. It excludes zero and burn addresses, Hook, PoolManager, custody, Operations, Treasury, Programmable, launch contracts, and historical role holders while allowing contract holders to receive native ETH at their own addresses, with bounded native payout simulation before claim. It evaluates recipient count, measured gas, gas-price cap, native balance, and transaction count before claim. Edge case: a reorg, incomplete or unordered logs, supply mismatch, missing source, or infeasible payout envelope prevents the claim.
REQ-eligibility-snapshot-1.measurement: Snapshot tests inject each log and reorg fault, compare deterministic manifests, prove supply reconciliation and hash recheck, and assert no claim request is prepared before the feasibility envelope passes.

REQ-epic-gate-1.title: Fail-closed epic-card hold policy
REQ-epic-gate-1.statement: Given a returned card and a buyback offer validated by REQ-collector-crypt-adapter-1, when the card is in the existing documented epic tier (`prizeTier === '1'`) and is eligible for sale, then it becomes a held position exactly when offerAtomic multiplied by 100 is less than insuredValueAtomic multiplied by 40; equality sells. Other documented tiers do not enter this 40-percent threshold branch. Missing or invalid data, missing mint, rarity conflict, buyback unavailable, changed quote, wrong mint, or an unverified insured-value reconciliation creates a HELD_* position, never auto-sells, raises an alarm, and records the card's attributed purchase-cost share, typed insured value or null, reason, evidence digest, and opening time. A held position is removed from the cycle's settled path, not from its attribution. Its owner decision is idempotent and bound to position ID, evidence digest, request ID, and position revision: `keep-holding` has no settlement effect, and `sell` starts its supplementary settlement. A held card does not independently block a new claim.
REQ-epic-gate-1.measurement: BigInt and lifecycle tests cover the prizeTier-1 strict inequality and equality, non-epic tier behavior, every fail-closed HELD_* class, immutable position evidence, insured-value reconciliation failure, per-position owner-decision idempotency, cycle completion with settled cards, and a held card that remains counted without independently refusing a new claim.

REQ-operations-wallet-1.title: Bounded Operations process claim
REQ-operations-wallet-1.statement: Given accrued process liability, when current Operations calls claimProcess(bytes32 cycleId, uint256 amountWei, address destination), then the hook accepts only a nonzero permanently unused cycleId, a positive amount no greater than both liability and remaining capacity, and destination equal to msg.sender. It debits and makes an exact native value call atomically, permanently records the cycleId, emits cycleId, amountWei, destination, timestamp, capWei, and usedAfterWei only after payment succeeds, and exposes remainingProcessClaimCapacity(). Edge case: a zero or reused cycleId, zero amount, wrong caller, third-party destination, excessive amount, failed transfer, or reentrancy leaves liabilities, history, and balances unchanged.
REQ-operations-wallet-1.measurement: Forge tests cover every authorization and amount boundary, transfer rollback, reentrancy, event fields, permanent cycle replay rejection, solvency before and after, and independent preservation of fee remainders.

REQ-policy-engine-1.title: Atomic policy controls and rehearsal mode
REQ-policy-engine-1.statement: Given an Operations-wallet cycle, when it reaches a claim, purchase, or signature boundary, then the policy engine atomically maps dashboard caps and allowlists to micro-USD controls, enforces a rolling 24-hour spend ledger, maximum cycles per day, per-cycle cap, rolling realized-plus-at-risk loss cap, maximum outstanding custody, and an execution pause or kill switch before every signature. It also admits a claim while open held positions remain unless their count is greater than or equal to `maxHeldPositions` or their value exceeds `maxHeldValueMicroUsd`; that refusal is `HELD_LIMIT`. Held value is attributed purchase cost in USD micro-units. Insured amounts remain informational and cannot replace that control value; neither a Solana stablecoin amount nor ETH wei is assumed to be USD. `maxHeldPositions` defaults to 10 with range 0 through 10, the verified capacity-safe maximum for the 16-entry DurableCycleStore; a configuration above 10 is refused until post-completion position archival or a measured store-capacity exemption exists. `maxHeldValueMicroUsd` defaults to `5000000000`. Pending epic decisions do not independently refuse a claim. Unattributed and unvalued custody remain fail-closed. It verifies all persisted purchase fields: unitPriceAtomic, quantity, totalAtomic, and boundedOverheadAtomic; enforces totalAtomic equals quantity multiplied by unitPriceAtomic; and reserves totalAtomic plus boundedOverheadAtomic. It evaluates finalized observed balances and obligations separately, with unresolved principal counted once. The existing USD outer rails remain 55 per unit, 165 per cycle and 495 per rolling day, with tighter owner limits preserved. Existing unit and aggregate Relay quote admission binds each USD valuation to the exact fetched request, quote digest, chain, asset, atomic amount and validity window, using integer decimal arithmetic with costs/exposure rounded up and proceeds rounded down. Committed spend remains at validated USD cost basis; unresolved liquid ETH or USDC exposure requires fresh bound valuation before additional risk and cannot double-count existing reservations. The policy separately checks exact ETH transaction maxima and the gas reserve. Missing valuation refuses new risk but not reconciliation or separately authorized recovery. The 250 USD test envelope limits external owner capital counted once, not recycled turnover or every production cycle. No second budget helper or onchain oracle is introduced. The first N production cycles require digest-bound manual approval. Cycle mode is persisted at creation and immutable; production and rehearsal services refuse the other mode. The production return minimum is the explicit TypedAmount {chainId: "4663", assetId: "native", decimals: 18, amountAtomic: "0"}; it means no general return minimum. No minimum or gas cap has an implicit atomic-unit default. Edge case: pause, cap breach, missing manual approval, held-position count or value limit, foreign mode, mismatched purchase arithmetic, placeholder minimum or gas cap, or unattributed or unvalued custody refuses the next irreversible action.
REQ-policy-engine-1.measurement: Policy and runner tests prove atomic cap application, rolling-window accounting, loss and custody limits, held-position count and value `HELD_LIMIT` refusal, a `maxHeldPositions` configuration at the 10/11/15/16 boundaries proving 10 accepted and every value above 10 refused, pending-decision non-refusal, purchase-field validation and reserve, observed-balance and obligation separation, pause-before-signature, digest binding, immutable mode isolation, explicit zero production return minimum, required gas-cap configuration, restart evidence, and no duplicate effect.

REQ-policy-engine-2.title: Pre-signature canaries and durable alerts
REQ-policy-engine-2.statement: Given any irreversible signature request, when the policy engine evaluates it, then it checks chain id, contract and proxy runtime hashes, native ETH identity and 18-decimal unit binding, funded native principal and distinct gas reserve, and bounded recipient-call feasibility, roles, protocol fee, router and quoter hashes, provider-policy digest, nonce or blockhash, gas reserves, pause and loss limits, and unattributed custody. A detected drift blocks signing, creates one durable deduplicated alert, and remains observable without exposing credentials. Edge case: any missing, stale, contradictory, or unverified canary result fails closed before a signature exists.
REQ-policy-engine-2.measurement: Canary tests inject each drift class and assert signature refusal, one persisted alert per condition, redaction, recovery only after the current evidence passes, and no duplicate alert across restart.

REQ-transaction-policy-1.title: Semantic transaction policy before external signing
REQ-transaction-policy-1.statement: Given a provider-produced EVM, Solana legacy, or Solana v0 transaction including address lookup tables, when a signature is requested, then the runner canonical validator schema hookemon.transaction-policy.v1 version 1 positively allowlists chain or program, target or selector, source, destination, mint, exact or bounded amount, value, gas, fee payer, co-signer, blockhash or deadline, priority fee, and absence of extra instructions. The adapters decoder must emit that identical canonical schema, not an adapter-only variant. Provider-specific Collector purchase and buyback policies are selected through a production binding loader and constructed separately, only from binding bytes independently digest-pinned against a separately trusted expected digest fixed before candidate acquisition, plus durable per-cycle facts and an independently observed RPC blockhash context; they are never constructed from candidate transaction semantics, and the candidate is used only by this same canonical decode/evaluate kernel. Purchase binds the admitted per-pack amount and durable request facts. Buyback additionally binds the independently finalized opened asset and owner, persisted quote and minimum, proceeds account, and separately authorized sell decision. Missing or mismatched binding authority refuses before durable intent or provider mutation. An isolated synthetic full-flow proof uses this same loader through the ordinary CLI and production execution machinery; synthetic binding authority cannot authorize live execution, and historical evidence-only bindings remain non-authoritative. No live provider binding values or expected digest are approved by this requirement. Every money minimum is an explicit TypedAmount. EVM per-transaction gas price cap and native reserve, and Solana priority-fee cap and lamport reserve, are required configuration fields. The literal atomic value '1' is a configuration error for any minimum or gas cap. The signed message is validated again before broadcast. There are exactly two signer identities, Operations EVM and Operations Solana; signing occurs outside the Node process unless a recorded owner exception applies. Edge case: an unknown target, mismatched address bytes, changed message, invalid co-signer, stale blockhash, missing gas cap, placeholder configuration, timeout, a provider-specific binding digest mismatch, an attempt to construct a provider-specific policy field from candidate-derived semantics, an attempt to use synthetic binding authority for live execution, or secret-bearing signer path refuses signing. Live Collector authority additionally requires exactly two immutable independently owner-approved purchase and buyback anchors authenticated by the frozen release manifest. Registry bytes, their adjacent digest, a configurable path, or environment selection cannot establish authority. All existing synthetic isolation and transaction validation rules remain enforced. Actual binding values and live transactions require separate explicit approval. The independently pinned Collector generatePack purchase profile additionally permits exactly compute-unit limit, provider-signed Memo, checked SPL transfer, and compute-unit price in that order. Its Memo appends the fixed :open suffix to the durable request memo; its checked transfer repeats the identical operator authority with identical signer and writable flags. For this profile, only the original candidate blockhash may be extracted to request independent RPC validity evidence. No candidate-derived validity claim is trusted, no block height is invented, and the original message bytes remain unchanged. RPC validity must be true for that exact blockhash at or above an immutable minimum observed slot. Recovery and pre-broadcast validation refresh that independent observation; the approval digest binds the immutable rule sidecar, including its minimum slot, so reconstruction cannot weaken it. Existing legacy purchase and buyback profiles remain unchanged.
REQ-transaction-policy-1.measurement: Negative fixtures for EVM and both Solana formats prove each allowlist field is enforced; configuration tests require each explicit minimum and gas cap and reject a literal atomic value '1'; parity fixtures prove the adapters decoder produces hookemon.transaction-policy.v1 version 1; signer tests prove external invocation, timeout visibility, two-identity separation, and pre-broadcast revalidation; provider-specific purchase and buyback policy fixtures prove refusal on a binding digest mismatch, on an unknown or malformed binding field, and on any factory input that carries candidate transaction bytes or decoded candidate semantics. Focused fixtures prove immutable binding authority across provider awaits, purchase binding to admitted per-pack facts, buyback binding to finalized open facts and a separately authorized sell decision, and refusal before intent or provider mutation when binding authority is absent or mismatched. An isolated ordinary-CLI full-flow fixture uses independently fixed synthetic bindings and isolated external services; negative fixtures prove that synthetic authority cannot enable live endpoints or live signer capabilities. This proof does not constitute approval of real provider binding values. Live registry tests accept only exact release-anchored stage bindings and reject missing approval evidence, modified paths or digests, substituted manifests, and synthetic/live mixing before mutation. Exact generatePack profile fixtures reject changed instruction order, Memo suffix, duplicate authority, signer flags, amounts, destinations, or missing/corrupt provider signatures. Independent RPC fixtures reject invalid or mismatched original hashes and regressing observation slots; recovery fixtures reject reconstruction with a lowered immutable minimum slot while preserving the original transaction message.
